paths_review.notes: Review of W7 (2671a6b..2a07000) and the A-7 recheck; fixes are in commit a42696a on the same branch. Everything I read line by line other than the fixed items was correct: util/fileio.hpp (UTF-16 surrogatepass, _wfopen, NUL/EINVAL, remove_file refusing a directory), the fspath.hpp bindings, the file sites in infra/types/tx/receiver_slot/api/picture/npz/wav/simfile, the codec glue's model paths, argparse's mutually exclusive groups (matches 3.13 take_action, usage and error order; 19 argv probes match except help text), test_dispatch_every_script, and the receiver_slot fast/slow split. The A-7 recheck holds up. tests/test_qrss_native_calibration.py compares Z bit for bit and the Gumbel constants to within 0.002 over 2400 Z. The ctest test_calibration.cpp draws an independent sample within 4 standard errors, and its TIMEOUT of 120 s against about 16 s measured is generous enough. Smaller things noted but not changed: types.cpp keeps a stale <fstream> include; util::list_dir sorts by bytes, while Python sorts by str, and the two differ only for names with surrogate escapes; the CLI's err stream is not tied to cout, so the interleaving on a shared terminal can differ; and stderr_text's held-back partial sequence is dropped if the process exits through std::exit mid-message. I did not touch receive.cpp; its matching --slot/--start fix is listed under shared_changes_needed.

findings.what: On POSIX, str(OSError)'s file name (common.cpp OsError) and argparse's invalid int/float/choice and ignored-explicit-argument values (argparse.cpp) took repr via pytext::decode, which reads a name's ED A0..BF xx bytes as one surrogate. They printed 'x\ud800.qrsp' where the scripts print 'x\udced\udca0\udc80.qrsp'. Both now use repr(pypath::fs_decode(...)), which is os.fsdecode.

sstvae-qrss transmit accepted a --slot that qrss_transmit.py refuses: with ED A0 80 between date and time, the C++ decoded a single surrogate, which fromisoformat accepts as the separator. Python holds three escapes and refuses. The slot is now parsed from pypath::fs_str(slot_text).
The same --slot/--start accept/refuse split exists in receive.cpp:291-302. Not changed because another agent owns that file; listed in shared_changes_needed.

pypath::with_name's ValueError text was '/ has an empty name'; pathlib says "PosixPath('/') has an empty name". The codec glue only passes .onnx names, so this path is unreachable from it. Fixed, with a test over every no-name path.

The codec bindings' translated() (codec/api.cpp, codec/codec.cpp) gained a catch of std::runtime_error in W7. pybind11's value_error, type_error and the like derive from it, so any of them thrown inside would have surfaced as RuntimeError. pybind11's builtin_exception is now rethrown before that catch. No current lambda throws one; this is hardening.

main.cpp's comment said Python's stdout is surrogateescape 'under a UTF-8 locale'. It is strict under en_US.UTF-8, and surrogateescape only in UTF-8 mode or under C, POSIX or C.UTF-8; stderr's encoding is also the locale's. Comment corrected; the behaviour difference is recorded as a deviation.

On POSIX, --callsign, --grid and --codec-id holding ED A0..BF xx still give a different refusal text (one surrogate against three escapes). Both implementations refuse. Left as a documented deviation because a clean fix needs separate str and byte forms through api.cpp's verbatim messages.

Windows narrow-path sites outside the QRSS scope: images.cpp (ifstream, stbi_write_png), codec.cpp:87 and grad_session.cpp:31 (byte-wise wstring), and checkpoint.cpp (narrow fs::path, getenv). Listed in shared_changes_needed.
